links.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic misrepresentation in GPT-4 generated clinical vignettes compared with US prevalence
links.effect: GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions and consistently produced vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations. No numeric effect sizes are given in the abstract.
links.quote: We found that GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing clinical vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations.

links.outcome: Change in differential diagnoses and plans when patient race, ethnicity, or gender varied in vignettes
links.effect: Differential diagnoses were more likely to include diagnoses that stereotype certain races, ethnicities, and genders. Plans showed significant association between demographic attributes and recommendations for more expensive procedures. No numbers are given in the abstract.
links.quote: The differential diagnoses created by GPT-4 for standardised clinical vignettes were more likely to include diagnoses that stereotype certain races, ethnicities, and genders.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of demographic and racial/gender bias in GPT-4 using clinical vignettes across diagnostic reasoning and treatment planning, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
